epithet: You are indeed one of the messengers
lede: A town that turned on its messengers, and one man who came running from its far side to defend them. The dead land brought to life; the sun running to its resting-place. And at the end a man holding a crumbled bone, asking who could ever give it life — and being answered.

names.name: Yā-Sīn
names.note: The two letters it opens with. Like the other letters at the heads of surahs, their meaning is known to Allah; Ibn al-Jawzī lists five sayings of the early commentators about these two, the best known being that of Ibn ʿAbbās and others — “O man”.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrimah, Qatādah and the majority; al-Qurṭubī calls it Makkan by agreement. Ibn al-Jawzī notes a report from Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah excepting one ayah (36:47), and a saying that the surah is Madinan, which the scholar who relayed it himself called “not well known”. Al-Qurṭubī also mentions that some connected its twelfth ayah with the Banū Salimah of Madinah. The traditional order places it forty-first.

evidence.quote: وَفِيها قَوْلانِ أحَدُهُما: أنَّها مَكِّيَّةٌ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، وقَتادَةُ، والجُمْهُورُ
سُورَةُ يس وَهِيَ مكية بإجماع. وهى ثلاث وثمانون آية

setting: The surah opens with an oath — by the wise Qurʾan — sworn to a single statement: “You are indeed one of the messengers, on a straight path.” Everything that follows supports it. It was sent to a man who had been called a liar by his own people for years, and to the small company that had believed him.

First comes a story for both. Messengers came to a town: two, then a third to strengthen them. Its people said what Quraysh said — you are only men like us; we see an ill omen in you; stop, or we will stone you. Then a man came running from the farthest part of the city. “My people, follow the messengers. Follow those who ask no wage of you, and are rightly guided.” The surah does not say how he died. It says only that he was told, “Enter the Garden,” and that his first thought was for those who had killed him: “If only my people knew how my Lord has forgiven me.” The Qurʾan names neither him nor the town; the commentators relate that he was called Ḥabīb, and many said the town was Antioch, which Ibn Kathīr gives reasons to doubt.

Then the signs, set out for people who think the dead stay dead: the dead earth made to live and yield grain; the night with the day stripped from it; the sun running to a resting-place appointed for it; the moon passing through its stations until it comes back like an old, curved palm-stalk.

The surah ends on a scene the commentators tie to a particular man. One of the chiefs of Quraysh — al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, or Ubayy ibn Khalaf — came to the Prophet ﷺ with a decayed bone, crumbled it in his hand, and said: “Muḥammad, will Allah raise this, now that it has rotted?” He said: “Yes. He will cause you to die, then raise you, then enter you into the Fire.” And the closing ayat came down: “He strikes a comparison for Us and forgets his own creation. He says: who will give life to bones when they are dust? Say: He will give them life who produced them the first time.”

occasions.title: The crumbled bone
occasions.text: Al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a decayed bone and crumbled it, saying: “Muḥammad, will Allah resurrect this after it has decayed?” He said: “Yes — Allah will resurrect this; He will cause you to die, then bring you to life, then enter you into the fire of Hell.” Then the ayat at the end of Yā-Sīn were revealed.
occasions.source: Ibn ʿAbbās: al-Ḥākim, who graded it ṣaḥīḥ; Ibn Kathīr gives it, and reports from Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah and others naming Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

aim: To establish the truth of the message and of the Resurrection, and the proofs of both.
themes: The truth of the Messenger ﷺ
Signs in the earth and sky

outline.title: The oath, and who will listen
outline.summary: Yā-Sīn. By the wise Qurʾan: you are indeed one of the messengers, on a straight path — a sending down from the Almighty, the Merciful, to warn a people whose fathers were not warned. Upon most of them the word has come true; it is the same whether you warn them or not. You warn only one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful unseen. It is We who give life to the dead, and record what they send ahead and the traces they leave.

outline.title: The people of the town
outline.summary: Set forth for them the example of the people of the town, when the messengers came to it: two, whom they denied, so We strengthened them with a third. A man came running from the farthest part of the city: “My people, follow the messengers. Why should I not worship Him who made me?” It was said: “Enter the Garden.” He said: “If only my people knew how my Lord has forgiven me.” After him We sent no host against his people; it was but a single cry, and they were extinguished. Alas for the servants: no messenger comes to them but they mock him.

outline.title: Signs
outline.summary: A sign for them is the dead earth: We give it life and bring grain out of it. A sign for them is the night: We strip the day from it. The sun runs to a resting-place of its own — that is the decree of the Almighty, the Knowing (36:38). The moon We have measured in stations, until it returns like an old date-stalk. It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outrun the day; each floats in an orbit. And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship.

outline.title: The single cry
outline.summary: When they are told, “Spend of what Allah has provided you,” the disbelievers say, “Shall we feed those whom Allah could feed if He willed?” They say, “When is this promise?” They await only a single cry that will seize them as they dispute. The Trumpet is blown, and from the graves they hasten to their Lord: “Woe to us — who has raised us from our sleeping-place?” This is what the Most Merciful promised.

outline.title: The two companies
outline.summary: The people of the Garden that Day are happily occupied — they and their spouses, in shade, on couches. “Peace”: a word from a Merciful Lord. “And stand apart today, you guilty. Did I not charge you, children of Ādam, not to worship Satan?” Today We seal their mouths; their hands speak to Us, and their feet bear witness to what they used to earn.

outline.title: Not poetry
outline.summary: We have not taught him poetry, nor would it befit him: it is only a reminder and a clear Qurʾan, to warn whoever is alive. Do they not see the livestock We made for them, which they own, ride and eat? Yet they have taken gods besides Allah. So let their words not grieve you.

outline.title: Who will give life to bones?
outline.summary: Does man not see that We created him from a drop — and there he is, an open adversary? He says, “Who will give life to bones when they have crumbled?” Say: He who produced them the first time. Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? His command, when He intends a thing, is only to say to it, “Be,” and it is. So glory to Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things; and to Him you will be returned.

keyAyah.why: The answer to every question about how. For the One who made the heavens and the earth, creation is a word.

virtues.text: Abū Dharr said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ in the mosque at sunset, and he said: “Abū Dharr, do you know where the sun sets?” I said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “It goes until it prostrates beneath the Throne. That is His saying: ‘And the sun runs to a resting-place of its own; that is the decree of the Almighty, the Knowing.’”

virtuesNote: This is among the most loved surahs of the Qurʾan, and much is repeated about it that is not established. The report that “everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qurʾan is Yā-Sīn” (al-Tirmidhī 2887) was called gharīb by al-Tirmidhī, who said one of its narrators is unknown; al-Albānī grades it fabricated. The instruction to recite it over the dying (Abū Dāwūd 3121, Ibn Mājah 1448) is weak in its chain. No sound hadith specifies a reward for reciting it on a particular night or for a particular need.
before: Fāṭir ended with those who swore that if a warner came to them they would be the best guided of peoples — and when he came, it only drove them further off (35:42). Yā-Sīn opens by swearing that he is that warner.
after: Yā-Sīn closes with the One whose command is “Be”. Al-Ṣāffāt opens with the angels ranged in ranks before Him, and the declaration: your God is One.

notable.label: We record what they send ahead, and their traces
The sun, the moon, and each in an orbit
“Peace” — a word from a Merciful Lord
Their hands speak, and their feet bear witness
